title: Configurable and Hierarchical Allreduce
event_hint: CHIARA exposes tunable batch-lane hierarchy and staged semi-composed Allreduce for hierarchical HPC systems
problem: MPI_Allreduce remains latency- and synchronization-sensitive for small and medium messages, where intra-domain communication is much cheaper than inter-domain traffic and conventional hierarchical implementations can centralize communication or reorganize data between Reduce-Scatter and Allgather.
mechanism: CHIARA groups ranks into tunable batches and lanes, stages the reduction vector so only bounded blocks are active, distributes inter-batch reduction/broadcast across rotating lane roots, and preserves a lane-aligned layout across Reduce-Scatter and Allgather. Independent intra-batch radices for both phases expose hierarchy and communication-depth trade-offs without centralized leaders.

evidence.claim: Against vendor MPI_Allreduce, CHIARA reaches up to 1.94x speedup on Polaris, 13.43x on Aurora, and 13.48x on Fugaku.
evidence.condition: CPU-resident collectives on Polaris, Aurora, and Fugaku; median runtime ratio
evidence.source_locator: PDF p.1 Abstract; p.10 Figure 11 and Section V-D

evidence.claim: In the parallel k-means application, CHIARA reduced iteration time from 10.32 s to 4.88 s at 576 ranks and from 11.20 s to 5.04 s at 2,304 ranks on Fugaku.
evidence.condition: Lloyd-style MPI+OpenMP k-means; 10 runs after 2 warmups
evidence.source_locator: PDF p.10 Section VI; lines reporting Fugaku iteration times

evidence.claim: The algorithm targets the small-to-medium regime of roughly 64 B to 32 KB per rank, where synchronization depth and locality boundaries dominate more than peak bandwidth.
Evaluation uses CPU-resident MPI at full node concurrency, with contiguous rank placement mapped to intended locality domains and each runtime reported as the median over 50 iterations.
For very large messages, CHIARA speedups approach 1 as bandwidth dominates and vendor baselines approach peak throughput.

evaluation_context: Microbenchmarks run on Polaris (Cray Slingshot 11, AMD EPYC), Aurora (Cray Slingshot 11, Intel Xeon Max), and Fugaku (A64FX, Tofu-D), with one rank per core and 50-iteration medians. The k-means case uses synthetic repeatable communication volumes and evaluates 256/2,048 ranks on Polaris and 576/2,304 on Fugaku.
limitations: The strongest gains are platform- and message-size-dependent; speedups diminish toward bandwidth-dominated large messages. The reported application study is MPI+OpenMP k-means with synthetic inputs, not a production deep-learning workload. Parameter selection is tuned per platform/workload, and the paper does not establish benefits for GPU/NCCL collectives or irregular communication patterns.
project_relevance: CHIARA is a useful reference for exposing topology and communication-stage choices as tunable policy rather than hiding them inside a fixed collective. Its batch-lane decomposition and bounded staged working set may inform AI-cluster collective design, but applicability to GPU/NCCL or KV-cache traffic requires separate measurements.
source_notes: The arXiv v1 PDF and all three referenced chunks were fetched; evidence locators refer to PDF pages, sections, and figures.
Platform-specific and workload-specific conditions are retained for all reported speedups.
